answer: Reputation inheritance must be explicitly forbidden at registration, meaning no new agent may claim a predecessor's earned standing. Each registrant locks a stake and attests only its own history, while peers may slash any identity that presents inherited credentials. A forger cannot reuse one reputation across many keys, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes. An honest cluster binds its reputations to distinct falcon-attested roots, whereas a farm reuses one summit of trust across many canyon-deep aliases. The defence forces attack cost to scale with identity count, pricing fakes out.
